According to reports, Apple has cut orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max due to "weak demand". A recent report from Nikkei Asia indicates that Apple has notified some suppliers to reduce component production for these two models, with the price increase said to have "hit consumer demand".

Price increase reportedly suppresses iPhone 18 Pro demand

The report cited "multiple sources familiar with the matter" and noted that Apple has "adopted a more cautious stance on shipments since early September". Two of the sources said that component orders for October were cut "by at least 15%" compared to Apple's original request.

Another supply chain manager who did not wish to be named told Nikkei Asia that demand is "not as strong as when all new models were launched simultaneously in the past". This is, of course, related to the fact that Apple will not unveil the standard iPhone 18 until next spring. However, suppliers also pointed out that this factor alone is not enough to fully explain the weak demand.

Comment posted by Hallmark

Every time we hear these kinds of "reports" about production cuts, when the financial figures come out, they turn out to be record-breaking quarters.

Every time there are reports of weak demand this year, Apple's revenue has actually continued to grow.

Unless the actual numbers reflect it, I won't easily believe these kinds of "reports".

One of the sources added that the "iPhone Duo" is also expected to face "a similar fate" after launch, meaning it may also see production cuts.

Apple priced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max 100 USD higher than the previous generation. Although the price increase has slowed demand, the report also pointed out that the demand slowdown "may not immediately translate into a decline in Apple's revenue".

Apple will release its fourth-quarter results for fiscal year 2026 on Monday, November 6, at which time there will be an initial understanding of the market demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max during the initial sales period.
